Consider carefully: if you find it hard to keep procedures consistent amid conflict, risk of violence and strict deadlines, are sensitive to long periods of standing and walking and to outdoor weather of all kinds, or are unwilling to document according to established rules and to testify in court when necessary, the actual work will differ from your expectations.

The work of customs and border protection officers can be divided into three connected but distinct work areas. The first is inspection and interviews: examining immigration applications, visas and passports and conducting interviews to determine eligibility for entry, stay and travel; inspecting inbound or outbound goods, baggage and personal effects for compliance with tax law and customs rules; and drawing product samples for testing and determining the duties and taxes owed. The second is investigation and handling: locating and seizing contraband, undeclared merchandise and the vehicles, aircraft or vessels concealing them; detaining people who violate customs or immigration law and arranging legal actions such as deportation; and bringing civil and criminal proceedings and collaborating with other enforcement agencies on investigation and prosecution. The third is recording and giving evidence: recording and reporting duty activities, findings, transactions, violations, discrepancies and decisions; explaining laws and regulations to travelers, prospective immigrants, shippers and manufacturers; and testifying at immigration appeals or in federal court about the relevant decisions, as well as reviewing refund applications and applications for penalty relief or mitigation. The three work areas alternate, but their basis, responsibility and risk differ; so do the procedures, authorization and risks across settings such as port inspection, border-area patrol, investigative evidence gathering and equipment inspection.

This table compares customs and border protection officers with the adjacent occupations of compliance managers, compliance officers, environmental compliance inspectors, and government property inspectors and investigators across seven items — core purpose, main objects and basis, core process, main outputs, responsible party, collaboration and supervision, and boundary of conclusions: adjacent occupations all involve checking rules and inspecting, but the objects, whether the role carries enforcement and seizure authority, and whether it carries management and prosecution or evidentiary responsibility do not shift just because the occupations are adjacent; compare item by item against actual duties and the process you work in.
Core purpose

Conduct inspection and investigation as people, conveyances, goods and merchandise enter or leave the country or move between states, detect violations of immigration and customs law and handle them according to law, leaving traceable enforcement records.

Core purposes of adjacent occupations: compliance managers plan and coordinate organizational activities to ensure compliance with ethical or regulatory standards; compliance officers review, assess and investigate the compliance of contracts, permits and licenses, among others; environmental compliance inspectors inspect and investigate pollution sources to protect the public and the environment and ensure compliance with regulations; government property inspectors and investigators investigate or inspect government property for compliance with contractual agreements and government rules.
Main objects and basis

People, conveyances, goods and merchandise entering the country or moving between states, declaration documents and case materials; the basis is immigration and customs laws and regulations, tax and duty rules, enforcement procedures and authorization, and the employer's direction and escalation paths.

Objects and basis of adjacent occupations: organizational compliance systems and regulatory standards (compliance managers), the compliance conditions of contracts and permits (compliance officers), pollution sources and environmental regulations (environmental compliance inspectors), government property and contractual agreements (government property inspectors and investigators).
Core process
Accept declarations → inspect and interview → determine compliance or eligibility → seize, detain and refer → record and report → testify and give evidence according to law.

Processes of adjacent occupations: formulate and implement compliance policies (compliance managers), accept, review and investigate compliance matters (compliance officers), inspect sites and investigate pollution and issue opinions (environmental compliance inspectors), inspect government property and investigate contract performance (government property inspectors and investigators).
Main outputs
Inspection and interview conclusions, seizure and detention records, duty and tax calculations, case materials and courtroom testimony.

Outputs of adjacent occupations: compliance policies and risk assessments (compliance managers), compliance review and investigation conclusions (compliance officers), environmental inspection reports and rectification opinions (environmental compliance inspectors), property and contract inspection reports (government property inspectors and investigators).
Responsible party

Staff in this occupation are responsible for the accuracy of inspection conclusions, the lawfulness of handling procedures, and the truthfulness and completeness of records; detention, referral and prosecution must be carried out according to law and within the chain of authorization and command, not decided unilaterally by them.

Responsible parties of adjacent occupations: compliance managers are responsible for compliance policies and their implementation; compliance officers for review and investigation conclusions; environmental compliance inspectors for inspection conclusions and rectification opinions; government property inspectors and investigators for inspection and investigation conclusions.
Collaboration and supervision

The scope of collaboration with the relevant authorities is to be verified against the applicable jurisdiction, actual duties and chain of command. Editorial check suggestion: verify the agency's anomaly reporting, handover, safety protection and the conditions for pausing/resuming specific actions; actions beyond your authority or lacking the necessary basis must not be carried out, and the remaining duties are performed under valid procedures and the instructions of authorized personnel, without unilaterally suspending all on-site tasks.

Collaboration of adjacent occupations: compliance managers collaborate with business and management; compliance officers collaborate with business departments and regulators; environmental compliance inspectors collaborate with environmental protection departments and the units being inspected; government property inspectors and investigators collaborate with procurement and contract departments.
Boundary of conclusions

Similar job titles do not mean the same duties: whether the focus is port inspection and immigration and customs enforcement, organizational compliance management, review of compliance matters, pollution and permit inspection, or government property and contract inspection — and whether the role carries enforcement authority, seizure authority, or management and prosecution or evidentiary responsibility — determines the scope of duties and how performance is assessed, and the roles cannot be swapped by title.

The preparation levels and authorization conditions of adjacent occupations do not apply to this occupation; verify them item by item against each occupation's official materials and the requirements of your employer.
Key occupational judgments

Six recurring professional judgments: whether personal documents and goods declarations are verified as consistent; whether inspections and interviews are conducted lawfully and according to procedure; whether duty activities, findings, violations and discrepancies are recorded truthfully and completely; whether seizure, detention and referral have a lawful basis and fall within authorization; whether the calculation and handling of duties, taxes and refund applications comply with the rules; and whether, when something exceeds your authority, evidence is insufficient or procedures conflict, it is reported, handed over and documented according to procedure.
Verify that personal documents, visas and passports and goods declarations are consistent; inconsistency leads to wrongful release, incorrect assessment or exemption, or inspection failures.

Conduct inspections and interviews according to enforcement procedures, explain the basis and inform the parties of the relevant rights and obligations; deviating from procedure makes the handling invalid or gives rise to disputes.
Record duty activities, findings, transactions, violations, discrepancies and decisions; missing or inaccurate records affect case handling, traceability and the giving of evidence.
Seizure, detention and referral must have a lawful basis and fall within the scope of authorization; acting beyond authority brings legal liability and evidentiary defects.

In the United States, customs and border protection officers correspond to O*NET-SOC 33-3051.04 (Customs and Border Protection Officers). The official scope is: conducting investigation and inspection as people, conveyances, goods and merchandise enter the country or move between U.S. states, in order to detect violations of immigration and customs laws and regulations; it does not include adjacent occupations such as compliance inspection or customs brokerage. values: Fictional port inspection scenario material (exercise input)

Fictional scenario: a customs and border protection officer encounters four problems while on duty. First, a traveler's declared items do not match the actual contents of the carry-on baggage; second, a shipment's declared classification looks suspicious and the duty owed needs to be determined; third, a colleague becomes emotionally agitated during questioning and refuses to cooperate; fourth, a record forwarded by a coworker lacks the inspection process and the actions taken.

Materials provided: key points of inspection and interview procedures; declaration and classification verification requirements; key points of seizure and detention procedures; duty activity and record standards.

Materials not provided: the final determination rules when declarations are inconsistent, who holds decision authority in classification disputes, the scope of authorization for coercive measures when cooperation is refused, and the division of responsibility for completing records. If the exercise requires these conditions, state your assumptions and the people you need to confirm with.
Task requirements

Please write a one-page handling and reporting plan covering: verification and handling recommendations when the declaration is inconsistent, verification and duty judgment for a suspicious classification, procedural handling of a subject who refuses to cooperate, and completing and verifying incomplete records.
The plan must state which information comes from the given materials and which is still assumption, and indicate whether the basis is inspection procedure, regulations or record standards.
Reference deliverable (can be derived from the prompt)

The plan should include: inconsistent declaration (re-verify documents and declaration information according to the verification requirements, do not take action yet, explain the verification process to the person and handle according to procedure), suspicious classification (verify product attributes and the basis according to classification requirements, handle tax-related judgments according to procedure, and refer disputes to the authorized position for a decision), refusal to cooperate (handle according to enforcement procedure and safety rules, request support when necessary, and do not use coercive measures beyond your authority), incomplete records (complete the inspection process and the actions taken, verify whether the change was implemented, and do not guess at missing content), and handover (state the status of the four items, the actions taken and the matters still to be confirmed).
The reference deliverable only lists the elements that should be included and does not require wording identical to the example; being able to explain the basis for your judgments is enough.
Boundaries and conclusions that cannot be inferred

This item only tests awareness of information verification, procedure compliance, on-site handling and reporting; it does not evaluate whether the handling of any real case is lawful, and it does not constitute a compliance determination, liability determination or legal advice.

Do not use real personnel data or unredacted personal information; where real inspection, seizure and personal information protection are involved, the law, competent-authority rules and unit policies must be followed.

entries.answer: Conduct inspection and investigation as people, conveyances, goods and merchandise enter the country or move between states: examining immigration applications, visas and passports and conducting interviews to determine eligibility for entry, stay and travel; inspecting goods, baggage and personal effects for compliance with tax law and customs rules; locating and seizing contraband and undeclared merchandise; detaining violators and arranging legal action; explaining laws and regulations; determining the duties and taxes owed and drawing samples for testing; recording and reporting duty activities, findings and decisions; bringing proceedings and collaborating with other enforcement agencies; and testifying at immigration appeals or in federal court.
entries.question: What does the daily work of a customs and border protection officer involve?

entries.answer: This occupation centers on port inspection and immigration and customs enforcement, carrying enforcement and seizure authority; compliance managers center on organizational compliance systems and risk management; compliance officers center on reviewing and investigating compliance matters such as contracts and permits; environmental compliance inspectors center on inspecting pollution sources and environmental regulations; government property inspectors and investigators center on government property and contract inspection; customs brokers act on the importer/exporter side to handle customs clearance and do not carry enforcement or seizure authority. Similar titles do not mean duties or authorization can be swapped.
entries.question: What is the difference between this occupation and adjacent compliance, inspection and customs brokerage positions?

entries.answer: Imaging detection, risk scoring and merchandise classification systems, regulatory knowledge bases and record drafting tools can reduce some matching, classification and recording work; but eligibility judgments in inspection and interviews, on-site handling and seizure of contraband, the legal basis for detention and referral, dispute handling on duties and taxes, and courtroom testimony still depend on people and remain constrained by enforcement procedure and authorization boundaries. O*NET shows 50% highly automated, 25% moderately automated and 11% slightly automated for this occupation; technical exposure is not the same as organizational adoption or the disappearance of jobs.

entries.answer: What can be verified is change at the task level: three types of task — inspection and risk prompts, merchandise classification and duty and tax calculation, and recording and case file organization — can be partly handled by tools; this page has no occupation-specific adoption or displacement data.

entries.answer: Lawful inspection and interviews, judging the lawfulness of on-site handling and seizure, the legal basis for detention and referral, duty, tax and refund handling, and the ability to record, report and give evidence according to procedure.

description.text: Customs and Border Protection Officers (O*NET-SOC 33-3051.04) conduct investigation and inspection as people, conveyances, goods and merchandise enter the country or move between states, in order to detect violations of immigration and customs law: covering examining immigration applications and documents and conducting interviews, inspecting goods, baggage and personal effects, locating and seizing contraband and undeclared merchandise, detaining violators and arranging legal action, explaining laws and regulations, determining duties and taxes and drawing samples, recording and reporting duty activities and decisions, and testifying in court when necessary; it should be noted that their U.S. wage, employment and industry data are published on O*NET under the parent occupation "Police and Sheriff's Patrol Officers" (33-3051.00), including the 2025 median annual wage of 76,210 dollars (36.64 dollars/hour), about 698,800 people employed in 2024, a 2024—2034 employment projection of average (3%—4%), an estimated annual average of about 53,700 openings including growth and replacement, industry concentration in government (95%), the interest code CER, and the occupation-level wage gap for mainland China together with control points for inspection authorization, detention and referral, and record-keeping.

subject.name: Customs and Border Protection Officers
subject.summary: In the United States, customs and border protection officers correspond to O*NET-SOC 33-3051.04 (Customs and Border Protection Officers), responsible for conducting investigation and inspection as people, conveyances, goods and merchandise enter the country or move between U.S. states, in order to detect violations of immigration and customs laws and regulations: examining immigration applications, visas and passports and conducting interviews to determine eligibility for entry, stay and travel; inspecting inbound or outbound goods, baggage and personal effects for compliance with tax law and customs rules; locating and seizing contraband, undeclared merchandise and the vehicles, aircraft or vessels concealing them; detaining people who violate customs or immigration law and arranging legal actions such as deportation; explaining laws and regulations to travelers, prospective immigrants, shippers and manufacturers; determining the duties and taxes owed and drawing product samples for testing; recording and reporting duty activities, findings, transactions, violations, discrepancies and decisions; and testifying at immigration appeals or in federal court about the relevant decisions. The preparation level for this occupation is Job Zone Three (SVP 6.0 to below 7.0); on O*NET its wage, employment and industry data are published under the parent occupation "Police and Sheriff's Patrol Officers" (33-3051.00), not values collected separately for this subcategory. Comparable positions in China are customs, exit and entry border inspection and port enforcement positions; their duties and authorization basis do not correspond one-to-one with this U.S. occupational subcategory and cannot be interchanged.
